benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Brent (January contract) settled down 3.5% at $89.37/bbl on 23 Nov (Rigzone, citing Reuters pricing), from about $92.57 a week ago, as traders unwound hedges against a feared weekend US escalation against Iran after Trump signaled more time for diplomacy (while saying he could resume the war next year if talks fail). Brent is down about 24% from a late-October high above $117 (Gulf News).

source.name: Rigzone (Reuters) — Oil Falls as Trump Signals Iran Talks

note: Brent settled down 3.5% at $89.37/bbl and WTI down 4.5% at $80.17/bbl on 23 Nov as traders unwound hedges against a feared weekend US escalation against Iran, after Trump signaled more time for diplomacy with Tehran (Rigzone, citing Reuters pricing). Brent is down about 24% from a late-October high above $117. Kpler data cited by Gulf News put Middle East crude exports at 18.99 million b/d in October, above the pre-war average of 18.56 million b/d, even as Hormuz-specific flows slipped toward about 10 million b/d by 10 Nov from 13.4 million at the start of the month. TTF rose about 3% to roughly €91/MWh on colder weather forecasts; JKM and Henry Hub were little changed.
